why: The core is meant to hold non-corporate, non-empire perspectives: the standpoint of people speaking from their own situation. A source enters the core (grown reading, associates, standpoints) only on evidence ABOUT THAT DOCUMENT. A label applied to a folder is not evidence about a document (policy v1 trusted such a label and admitted 1,025 documents of a mixed library about colonialism; see colonial-studies-audit.json). Fail closed: no document-level evidence means control. (Revision: the 28 curated primary works and the SAHO archive carried no label and were excluded by v1; they are the collection's intended voices.)

collections.20-first-person-voices: frontmatter perspective must be non-empty AND is declared per file (the 90 declared files carry different values: the interviewees' own first person, the author's own first person, children, older people, mentally ill, unhoused, imprisoned, atrocity survivors, ...)

explicit.11-multi-language/dialects-pidgins-creol: community voices: the transcript is the speakers' own speech (African American speakers in DC, Princeville, Rochester); CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; no frontmatter, so admitted by name
explicit.21-anti-colonial/dloc-oral-histories: interviews: the interviewee's own account, admitted by what the documents are, NOT by the folder-level label; includes 15 interviews with a no-redistribution notice (read locally for statistics, nothing published)
explicit.21-anti-colonial/saho-archive: South African History Online (62 files, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0): histories, biographies and tributes of the liberation struggle, written within the South African liberation-heritage project, not individual first-person accounts; admitted as the struggle's own record, PROPOSED: approve or amend

explicitPatterns.why: the 28 individually curated primary works at the top of 21-anti-colonial (Walker's Appeal, Cugoano, Cuffe, Pennington, Nat Turner, Garvey, Hayford, Lajpat Rai, Dutt, Naoroji, Apess, Pauline Johnson, Pokagon, Kartini, Aguinaldo, Mabini, Plaatje, J. J. Thomas, Sun Yat-sen, Marti, ...): works BY colonized, enslaved or Indigenous authors, chosen one by one. They carry no `perspective` field, which is why policy v1 excluded them while admitting the folder-labelled library. PROPOSED by the model that wrote this policy from titles and authors: approve or amend.

control: 21-anti-colonial/colonial-studies (1,025 English documents): a library about colonialism from every side; the 'colonized peoples' perspective is the folder's, identical on every one of its 1,058 labelled files; control until its documents are classified by the author's standpoint (gold/colonial-studies-audit-sample.md)
06-government-legal (the Declaration itself is the ground by decision, not by this gate)
limits: The label is still the curator's, not an independent verification of anyone's standpoint, wherever it is declared per file. 119 files in 20-first-person-voices declare nothing and stay controls. The 15 restricted interviews are admitted for reading, not for redistribution.
